claims.text: The ball-milled Mg-Al-Ti-V-Fe-Co powder is a BCC solid solution.
Ball milling may cause surface oxidation of the Mg-Al-Ti-V-Fe-Co powder.
SPS at 900–1000 °C, 30–50 MPa, and 10–15 minutes is an appropriate processing window for this alloy.
Sintering at 900–1000 °C activates sufficient diffusion for secondary-phase nucleation in Mg-Al-Ti-V-Fe-Co.
Sintering in this window precipitates fine, coherent, BCC-based intermetallic phases within the BCC matrix.
The secondary phases are likely Mg-rich or Al-rich Laves phases or B2-ordered structures.
A dense, continuous Al2O3/MgO oxide scale forms during sintering.
The secondary precipitates impede the diffusion of oxygen and metal cations.
The secondary precipitates increase hardness through precipitation hardening.
The Al2O3/MgO scale improves corrosion resistance.
Mg and Al have sufficiently high diffusivity at 900–1000 °C to overcome the kinetic barrier to secondary-phase nucleation.
Secondary-phase precipitation consumes excess chemical potential and consequently slows Mg loss and oxygen ingress.
The proposed processing window will produce density above 95% of theoretical density.
Vickers hardness will increase by 20–40% relative to the as-milled state.
Corrosion current density will decrease by one order of magnitude.
After 100 hours at 400 °C in air, the protective oxide scale will be less than 1 µm thick.
Above 1020 °C, rapid Mg evaporation causes Mg depletion, destabilizes the BCC matrix, and prevents formation of the protective oxide scale.
Below 850 °C, diffusion is insufficient for precipitate nucleation, producing a porous and weak microstructure.
A parabolic oxidation rate law indicates diffusion-controlled oxidation through a barrier.
Increasing Al content promotes BCC-phase formation in related CoFeNi- and CoCrFeNi-based alloys.

contradictions.description: The baseline states that temperatures above 1000 °C cause excessive Mg loss, whereas the boundary places failure only above 1020 °C, leaving the 1000–1020 °C interval inconsistently classified.
The baseline identifies insufficient diffusion below 800 °C, while the boundary states that all temperatures below 850 °C are insufficient, giving inconsistent lower thresholds.

The processing atmosphere is selected to minimize oxidation, yet the structural mediator states that a dense oxide scale forms during sintering; the experiment instead evaluates scale formation during a subsequent 400 °C air exposure.
